newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank cuts deposit and lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank cuts deposit and lending rates.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Thursday cut its deposit and lending rates by 50 basis points to 3.75 percent and 5.25 percent respectively as widely expected by the financial markets.
The repo rate, the central rate in the Riksbank's three tier system, currently stands at 4.35 percent after being cut by 25 basis points nine days ago.
The deposit and lending rates, that mark the floor and ceiling of the Riksbank's interest rate corridor, were last lowered on October 24.
The bank said the move would come into effect on December 11.
The move was widely expected by the financial markets.
A Reuter poll this week found 12 of 17 economists questioned expected the Riksbank to lower the interest rate corridor by 50 basis points.
"The cut was expected with both low inflation expectations and low inflation facilitating it," Tomas Pousette, Nordbanken economist told Reuters.
The Riksbank said the inflation outlook was good and in line with the government's target of two percent with flexibility of one percentage point either way.
"The conditions for inflation in line with the inflation target are still considered to be good," the bank said in a statement.
"The continued analysis of the outlook for inflation will be crucial for the construction of monetary policy:

Economists were now expecting a further cut to the repo rate this month, forecasting another cut of up to 25 basis points on December 17 when the bank sets a reverse repurchase operation that will last for three weeks.
The Riksbank will also present its last inflation report for the year on that day.
